_doc: BOOK'S PHONE — the read-only screen the loop is legible on. P opens it and cycles LONGHORN -> BOONE -> WALLET -> closed. It reports; it never acts. Every string and every measurement the panel draws lives here so the copy can be rewritten without touching scripts/systems/phone.gd. Read once at boot by that file.
_refresh_hz: The screen is a report, not an instrument: 4 Hz is faster than a reader's eye and 15x cheaper than per-frame. Nothing here is allocated while the phone is shut.
_candy: Candyland's pink. Held here so the wardrobe/Slab copy has one source if the phone ever speaks for that side of the fiction.
_app_speaker: = repo_orders.gd APP and mission_kit's dispatcher voice (D-063). The phone shows the LAST line this speaker said; the dispatcher is the app, never a named person.
foot_wallet: Balance is informational. Ask the app.
no_push: No push on file. The app is not saying.
idle: No open orders. Stay quiet and the app will find you.
rank_top: TOP RANK. There is nothing above PARTNER but Bolo.
boone_none: No paper with Boone. Appreciate you!
feed_none: Nobody has said anything to you.
_due_pattern: repo_orders.json's app_push is the only place the days and the amount of a live order exist as text -- repo_orders.gd holds them in locals, never in fields (repo_orders.gd:377-381). The phone recovers them from the push it is already showing. If app_push's wording changes, change this pattern; no code edit.
_paper_scan: How far back the phone will look for the ORDER push that carries the days and the amount. Twelve app lines is roughly one order's worth of chatter; beyond that the phone would be quoting paper from a job two orders ago.
_tell_min_prefix: paper_tells in repo_orders.json carry {placeholders}; the phone matches on the literal text BEFORE the first brace, and refuses a prefix shorter than this so a common phrase can never false-flag clean paper. 'DAYS PAST DUE: ' (with the colon) is 15 and does not appear in a clean push.
